description: Nucleoid fills a missing configuration value once without replacing supplied laws
code:
source = 4
config = {}
config.limit ??:= source
assert(config.limit, 4)
source = 9
assert(config.limit, 4)
config.limit = source * 2
config.limit ??:= missing
source = 6
assert(config.limit, 12)
config.limit

description: Nucleoid distinguishes false zero empty text and NaN from nullish targets
code:
flag = false
flag ??:= missing
zero = -0
zero ??:= missing
text = ""
text ??:= missing
number = Number.NaN
number ??:= missing
assert(flag, false)
assert(1 / zero, Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY)
assert(text, "")
assert(Number.isNaN(number), true)
[flag, text]

description: Nucleoid isolates a conditional fill from the standing rule that executes it
code:
paid = false
fallback = 3
chosen = null
if paid: chosen ??:= fallback
paid = true
assert(chosen, 3)
fallback = 8
chosen = null
assert(chosen, null)
paid = false
paid = true
assert(chosen, 8)
fallback = 12
assert(chosen, 8)
chosen

description: Nucleoid retains constructor target naming and lazy one-shot effects
code:
count = 0
class Item(n):
    this.n = n
    count := count + 1
selected = null
selected ??:= Item(n=5)
assert(selected.id, "selected")
assert(selected.n, 5)
assert(count, 1)
selected ??:= Item(n=9)
assert(count, 1)
assert(Item.length, 1)
selected.n
